BA.definition: An exclamation used 1. to startle people, or 2. to make a child laugh by pretending to startle him. (In sense 2, it follows the exclamation IT.)

BAAG.definition: To wear a G-string, loincloth, or breechclout.

BAAK.definition: Old, aged: said of rice, tobacco, wine, etc.
To age, to keep (rice, tobacco, wine, etc.) for a period of time.
BAAK.ilok_example: Baakem nga nalaing dayta basi tapno naimimas.
BAAK.eng_example: Keep that wine for some period of time so that it will improve in taste.

BAAW.eng_example: The rice is not hot anymore.

BAAW.definition: 1. To lose heat; to cool off. 2. To abate, decrease, go down (as fever, anger, etc.).
BAAW.ilok_example: Bimmaaw met la ti gurigor na.

BABA.definition: 1. Any place down or under something. 2. Downstairs.
1. To become low or lower, to go down. 2. To go or come down or downstairs, to descend.
BABA.ilok_example: Bimmaba ti presio ti bagas ita nga bulan.
BABA.eng_example: The price of rice went down this month.

BABA.definition: To take, bring, or carry down or downstairs.
BABA.ilok_example: Mangibaba kayo ti tallo nga baso ti danum.
BABA.eng_example: Bring downstairs three glasses of water.

BABAEN.definition: By means of, by the use of, through.
BABAEN.ilok_example: Nakapagadalak met laeng iti kolehiyo babaen ti tulong mo.
BABAEN.eng_example: I was able to study in college through your help.

BABAI.definition: 1. A female; woman, girl. 2. Mistress, concubine.
To have or keep a mistress or concubine.
BABAI.eng_example: Don’t keep a mistress because that’s bad.

BABAI.definition: To make or keep (someone) as one’s mistress or concubine.

BABAIN.ilok_example: Saan nak nga ibabain kadagiti gagayyem mo.
BABAIN.eng_example: Don’t shame me before your friends.

BABAIN.definition: To be shamed, disgraced, or embarrassed.

BABAK.definition: Sin, moral failure (used only in prayers).

BABALAW.definition: To criticize, correct, reprove, reprimand, censure.

BABARA.definition: To be feverish, hot with fever.

BABASA.definition: 1. To get oneself wet; to cause oneself to get wet, as when playing in or with water. 2. To become wet or moist.

BABASIL.definition: Whitlow or felon; an inflammation at the end of a finger near or under the nail.
To have a whitlow inflammation (said of a finger).

BABAWI.definition: To repent or regret what one has done.
BABAWI.eng_example: You will repent later but it will be late.

BABAWI.ilok_example: Isu ti nagbabawi ti iyaay na ditoy.
BABAWI.eng_example: It was he who regretted his having come here.

BABAWI.definition: To take back (what one has given away).

BABUMBABUY.definition: To move or walk on the hands and knees.
BABUMBABUY.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agbabumbabuy ta marugitan ta imam.
BABUMBABUY.eng_example: Don’t walk on your hands and knees for your hands will get dirty.

BABUY.definition: 1. Pig, hog, swine. 2. A person regarded as acting or looking like a pig; a dirty or filthy person.

BADANG.definition: A kind of large knife (BUNENG) or bolo with a pointless blade, shorter and much broader than the common knife.
To hit or threaten with a badang bolo.

BADDEK.definition: To step in or be present at (a place).
BADDEK.ilok_example: Saan ka nga bumaddek ditoy balay mi.
Saan mo nga baddeken ta mula.

BADO.definition: To put on one’s clothes or dress, to clothe or dress oneself.
BADO.eng_example: Put on your clothes for we are going.

BADO.definition: To dress (someone) with, to cause (someone) to wear.
BADO.ilok_example: Daytoy ti ibado na idiay kabsat na.
BADO.eng_example: This is what he will dress his brother (or sister) with.

BADUYA.definition: A kind of native rice cake which is flat and round.

BAED.definition: Talking through the nose, as one with a harelip.

BAEL.ilok_example: Isu ti nangibael kadagiti karga mi.
BAEL.eng_example: It was he who carried our load.

BAELAN.definition: To be able, competent, or fit (to do something).
BAELAN.eng_example: Are you able to drive a motor vehicle now?

BAET.definition: 1. To put, place, or go between. 2. To intervene, interpose.
BAET.ilok_example: Saan ka nga bumaet kadakami nga dua.
BAET.eng_example: Don’t place yourself between the two of us.

BAET.definition: 1. To put or place between. 2. To intercede or intervene for (someone).

BAETAN.ilok_example: Adayo ti kasilyas iti igid ti baetan.
BAETAN.eng_example: The toilet is far from the side of the main road.

BAGA.definition: 1. To tell, say, declare, utter. 2. To tell on, inform against.

phrases.phrase: No dika nga agsardeng, ibaga ka ken ni tatang ko.
phrases.translation: If you don’t stop, I’ll tell on you to my father.

BAGAS.definition: 1. Husked or polished rice. 2. Substance or content (of fruits); seed or kernel (of rice, corn, etc.); tuber or tuberous root (of potatoes, taro, etc.). 3. Substance, content, essence, meaning.

phrases.phrase: Awan pay ti bagas na dayta kamotit yo.
phrases.translation: Your sweet potatoes have no tuberous roots yet.

phrases.phrase: Ania ti bagas daydiay sinao na?
phrases.translation: What was the content of what he said?

BAGAS.definition: To have substance or content; to develop seeds, kernels, or tuberous roots.
BAGAS.eng_example: This corn is now developing seeds.
His prickly heat papules are so many.

BAGAY.definition: To adjust, fit; to make suitable, agreeable, or appropriate.
BAGAY.ilok_example: Ibagay mo ti bagim iti biag ditoy barrio.
BAGAY.eng_example: You adjust yourself to life in this barrio.

BAGBAG.definition: A leguminous tree with large, bright-red flowers whose leaves are supposed to cure headaches.

BAGBAGA.ilok_example: Bagbagaam dayta adim iti nasayaat nga aramid.
BAGBAGA.eng_example: Advise your younger brother (or sister) about good deeds.

BAGBAGUTOT.definition: A shrub which bears black, fleshy fruits which are edible.

BAGI.definition: 1. Share, portion, part, lot. 2. Child or children, offspring.

BAGI.eng_example: He was the one who represented us.

BAGKAT.definition: To lift up, carry, heave, raise up.
BAGKAT.eng_example: Would you like me to lift you up?

BAGKONG.definition: To stab, as with a dagger.

BAGNET.definition: To dry, to cause to become dry.
BAGNET.eng_example: Dry those pieces of wood well.

BAGNET.definition: Pieces of fat from which lard has been extracted.

BAGNOS.ilok_example: Ibagnos mo ida nga mapan idiay plasa.
BAGNOS.eng_example: Lead them in going to the plaza.

BAGSANG.definition: A kind of small, fat fish living either in the sea or at the mouth of rivers.

BAGTIN.definition: To lift up so as to estimate the weight.
BAGTIN.eng_example: Lift up and estimate the weight of my suitcase.

BAGYO.definition: Typhoon, storm, hurricane; strong, violent wind.
To have a typhoon, storm, or hurricane.
BAGYO.ilok_example: Agbagyo man siguron intono maysa nga bulan.
BAGYO.eng_example: Perhaps there will be a typhoon again next month.

BAGYO.definition: To be hit by a typhoon, storm, or hurricane.
BAGYO.eng_example: Our festival was hit by a typhoon.

BAGYO.definition: To be destroyed, demolished, felled, blown down, or carried away by a typhoon, storm, or hurricane.
BAGYO.eng_example: Our house was destroyed by a typhoon.

BAILITA.definition: The part of the rice plant with the grains that are cut and laid out on the rice field on top of the stubble to dry.

BAIN.definition: To be ashamed or feel embarrassed (to do something; to see or talk to someone).
BAIN.eng_example: I am ashamed to see you.

BAIN-BAIN.definition: Mimosa pudica; a thorny, creeping weed whose leaves are sensitive to touch.

BAIS.definition: To charge against what one owes.
BAIS.ilok_example: Ibais mo dagitoy innalak ti utang mo kanyak.
BAIS.eng_example: Charge these that I took against what you owe me.

BAKABAKA.ilok_example: Saan tayo nga mapan no agbakabaka ka.
BAKABAKA.eng_example: We won’t go if you are hesitant.

BAKAL.ilok_example: Saan mo nga ibakal dayta pungan.
Gumilgilang pay laeng ti apoy ti bakal.
BAKAL.eng_example: The flames of war are still burning.

BAKAL.definition: To engage in a war, a fight, or battle.
BAKAL.eng_example: It is hard to engage in a war.

BAKAL.definition: 1. To wage war at. 2. To throw stones at.

BAKARA.definition: A kind of small fish found at the mouths of rivers.

BAKAS.definition: To strip off some part of (a wall, roof, window, etc.).
BAKAS.ilok_example: Daytay napalabas a bagyo ti nangbakas iti balay mi.
BAKAS.eng_example: The past typhoon stripped off some parts of our house.
The store of Rose was unroofed.

BAKASYON.definition: To have a vacation, spend a vacation.
BAKASYON.eng_example: Let’s spend our vacation in Baguio.

BAKASYON.definition: To take on a vacation, to take to a place for a vacation.
BAKASYON.ilok_example: Ibakasyon ko daytoy baket ko idiay Amerika.
BAKASYON.eng_example: I’ll take my wife to the United States for a vacation.

BAKAT.definition: To leave a trace, mark, or impression.
BAKAT.ilok_example: Uray la nga nagbakat diay plantsa ti pudot na.
BAKAT.eng_example: The iron left a mark because of its heat.

BAKBAKETAN.definition: Very old, extremely old: said of the female.
BAKBAKETAN.eng_example: The one he married was extremely old.

BAKED.definition: 1. Stocky, heavily built, sturdy, muscular. 2. Nice, pleasing, exquisite.
BAKED.eng_example: It is nice to ride in an airplane.

BAKET.definition: Old in years: said of the female, especially women.
To grow old or older: said of the female.

BAKI.definition: Nest made by man for hens in which to lay and hatch their eggs.

BAKIG.definition: Ten units or heads (of cows, coconuts, etc., except persons, rice bundles, etc.).

BAKIR.definition: To cut trees in the forest.
BAKIR.eng_example: Let’s go cut trees in the forest.

BAKKA.definition: 1. A large, shallow earthen basin, used especially for washing and cleaning rice, fish, vegetables, etc. 2. (Figuratively) A very large vulva.

BAKLAY.eng_example: Carry that suitcase on your shoulder.

BAKNANG.definition: To become rich, wealthy, or affluent.

BAKRANG.definition: Side of man’s body extending from the armpit to the waist.
To feel pain or have pains at the side of one’s body.
BAKRANG.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agbagkat iti nadagsen tapno saan ka nga bakrangen.
BAKRANG.eng_example: Don’t lift heavy things so that you won’t have pains at the side of your body.

BAKTAW.eng_example: It was he who jumped over me.

BALA.definition: To put bullets in, to load: said of weapons.
To load with or in (as bullets), to use as a bullet.
BALA.ilok_example: Daytoy ti ibalam dita paltog mo.

BALABAG.definition: To hit with something, to throw or hurl something at.
BALABAG.eng_example: It was he who threw something at me.

BALABAL.ilok_example: Balabalan yo dayta ubing ti ules ket nalam-ek.
BALABAL.eng_example: Wrap a blanket around that child for it is cold.

BALABAL.definition: To wrap with, to use to wrap.
BALABAL.ilok_example: Dayta ules ti ibalabal yo kanyana.

BALABALA.definition: Thought, idea; guess, conjecture, surmise; apprehension, misgiving.
To guess, suppose, surmise; to be apprehensive that.
BALABALA.eng_example: He is apprehensive that they got lost.

BALAGTONG.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agbalagtong ta adda matmaturog.
BALAGTONG.eng_example: Don’t jump for someone is sleeping.

BALAKAD.ilok_example: Balakadam ida ta nasukir da unay.
BALAKAD.eng_example: Give them some advice for they are very disobedient.
Listen to the pieces of advice that they will give you.

BALAKI.definition: To turn to the opposite direction, as joy to sorrow.
BALAKI.ilok_example: Saan kay nga katawa nga katawa ta dinto agbalaki dagita katkatawa yo.
BALAKI.eng_example: Don’t laugh and laugh lest your laugh turn to sorrow.

BALANGEG.definition: A widely spreading water vine whose young leaves are eaten.

BALANGKANTIS.definition: 1. One who bargains hard all the time. 2. Deceitful.

BALASANG.definition: 1. Adult or mature female; woman. 2. Single or unmarried woman; spinster; maiden, virgin.
BALASANG.eng_example: Your daughter is already an adult.

BALASANG.ilok_example: Adda balbalsangen mi dita sumuno nga ili.
BALASANG.eng_example: There is someone whom we are wooing in the next town.

BALASBAS.definition: To trim, e.g. a log, bamboo, etc.
BALASBAS.ilok_example: Binalasbasan na daydiay pinukan mo nga kawayan.
BALASBAS.eng_example: He trimmed the bamboo that you felled.

BALASBAS.definition: To whip, beat, hit with a stick, a branch of a tree, etc.
BALASBAS.ilok_example: Saan mo nga balasbasan ta kabayo.

BALASITANG.definition: A young girl; synonym of BUMALASANG.

BALAT.definition: To throw down, as in judo or wrestling.

BALAW.definition: To wonder or take notice of something or a situation.
BALAW.eng_example: You may wonder about the situation but it is too late.

BALAW.definition: To take notice of, to wonder about.
BALAW.ilok_example: Isu ti nangbabalaw ti kaawan mo.
BALAW.eng_example: It was he who took notice of your absence.

BALAWBAW.definition: Awning, canopy, covering, especially of a cart.
To use an awning, canopy, or covering.
To provide (especially a cart) with an awning, canopy, or covering.

BALAY.definition: House, home; abode, residence, habitation, dwelling.
To build one’s house; to establish one’s home, residence, or dwelling place; to reside.
BALAY.ilok_example: Agbalay tayo idiay ili dagiti appo tayo.
BALAY.eng_example: Let’s reside in the town of our ancestors.

BALAY.definition: To curdle, coagulate, solidify (as lard or cooking in cold weather).

BALAYANG.definition: A variety of banana with thick skin and numerous seeds.

BALAYBAY.definition: To hang (usually articles of clothing) in order to dry, air, or screen off something.
BALAYBAY.ilok_example: Inka man ibalaybay daytoy nagsukatak idiay pagsalapayan ta nabasa ti ling-et.
BALAYBAY.eng_example: Will you please hang my clothes which I just changed on the clothesline for they are wet with perspiration.

BALBAL.definition: To rinse or wash lightly, clean with water.
BALBAL.eng_example: Clean the kitchen very well with water.

BALBALLUSA.definition: A spreading, spiny herb with white flowers and whitish-gray fruits; it resembles the eggplant.

BALDI.definition: A large can, either rectangular or cylindrical; a kerosene can.

BALE.ilok_example: Kayat na kano ti bumale iti dua nga kaha ti sigarilyo.
BALE.eng_example: He says he wants to buy on credit two packs of cigarettes.

BALEDIKTORIAN.definition: To become the valedictorian of a class.

BALENGBENG.definition: To hang, put, or use as a screen or curtain.
BALENGBENG.ilok_example: Isu ti mangibalengbeng ti daytoy idiay salas.
BALENGBENG.eng_example: It is he who will hang this (as screen or curtain) in the living room.

BALES.definition: To take revenge on someone; to repay someone.
To take revenge on; to repay, return the favor to.
BALES.eng_example: Why do you take revenge on me?

BALES.definition: To take revenge for; to repay (someone) for.
BALES.eng_example: It was he who took revenge for me.

BALES.definition: To seam and hem (a dress, etc.).

BALIBAD.definition: To pronounce wrongly, especially by interchanging the sounds; to mispronounce.
BALIBAD.ilok_example: Kanayon ko nga mabalibad ti nagan mo.

BALIKID.definition: The other side, the opposite or reverse side.
To turn or roll oneself sideways to the other side, to turn over.
BALIKID.eng_example: Please turn over for a moment.

BALIKID.definition: To turn or roll (someone or something in a resting position) sideways to the other side; to turn over.
BALIKID.ilok_example: Saan mo nga balikiden ta papel mo.

BALIKTAD.definition: 1. To turn the inside out. 2. To turn over.
BALIKTAD.ilok_example: Isu ti nangbaliktad ti libro na.
BALIKTAD.eng_example: It was he who turned over his book.

BALIKUTSA.definition: A coil of string of soft, white-yellowish sugar.

BALIN.ilok_example: Saan nga nagbalin ti luko na kanyak.
BALIN.eng_example: His foolishness was not effective on me.

BALIN.definition: To be possible or probable (followed by a sentence introduced by NGA).
BALIN.eng_example: It is possible that they will arrive today.
He is able to walk now.

BALIN.ilok_example: Saan nga mabalin ti luko na kanyak.
BALIN.eng_example: His foolishness is not effective on me.

BALIN.definition: To become, to grow, develop, or turn into (followed by a noun or adjective introduced by NGA).
BALIN.eng_example: My son turned into a lazy person.

BALINSUEK.definition: To put or place upside down.
BALINSUEK.ilok_example: Saan mo nga balinsueken ta anak mo.
BALINSUEK.eng_example: Don’t put your child upside down.

BALINSUEK.definition: To fall head first, upside down.

BALINTUAG.definition: To roll over, to cause to somersault, tumble, or rotate.

BALISONGSONG.definition: Funnel, cone, especially one made of paper or a leaf.
To make a funnel or cone, especially using a piece of paper or a leaf.
BALISONGSONG.eng_example: Do you know how to make a funnel?

BALISONGSONG.definition: To make or shape into a funnel or cone.

BALITI.definition: A tree (Ficus sp.) which gives valuable timber.

BALITUNGEG.definition: To be worm-eaten, to become affected with blight: said of the sweet potato (KAMOTIT).
BALITUNGEG.eng_example: Your sweet potatoes will become affected with blight again.

BALITUNGEG.definition: Worm-eaten, affected with blight: said of the sweet potato.
Any portion of the sweet potato that is affected with blight or is worm-eaten.
BALITUNGEG.ilok_example: Adu ti balitungeg na daytoy inted mo kanyak nga kamotit.
BALITUNGEG.eng_example: This sweet potato which you gave me has many worm-eaten parts.

BALIW.definition: To cross, go across, traverse; to come over.

BALIW.ilok_example: Ibaliw mo dayta maletak dita kalsada.
BALIW.eng_example: Carry my suitcase across the street.

BALKUT.definition: To wrap or bundle up things, especially one’s personal belongings or household effects.

BALLAAG.definition: Loud argument, loud voice or screams in an argument; cry for help.
To cry or scream for help.

BALLAET.definition: To insert in regular intervals, to intertwine in a regular pattern, to mix with according to a pattern.
BALLAET.ilok_example: Iballaet mo dagitoy puraw kadagita asul.
BALLAET.eng_example: Mix these white ones with those blue ones.

BALLAIBA.definition: Eel grass, tape grass; a common, edible, submerged, hydrocharitaceous, freshwater plant. Its leaves and roots (GURGURMOT) are eaten.

BALLAIBI.definition: To suffer from pains in the region of the spleen.
BALLAIBI.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agtaray-taray ta ballaibien ka.
BALLAIBI.eng_example: Don’t run back and forth for you will suffer from pains in the region of the spleen.

BALLASIW.definition: The opposite side (of), the place across (a river, a street, an ocean, etc.).
To take across or to the opposite side of, to go across with.

BALLATAD.definition: To throw a big knife (BUNENG) at someone.
To throw a big knife at, to hit with a big knife.
BALLATAD.ilok_example: No umasideg ka, ballataden ka iti daytoy iggem ko nga buneng.
BALLATAD.eng_example: If you come near, I’ll throw this big knife which I am holding at you.

BALLATIK.definition: To hit: said of a chip, a splinter, or a sliver.
To be hit by a chip, splinter, or sliver.
BALLATIK.eng_example: Your head was hit by a chip.

BALLIGI.definition: To win, be victorious or triumphant.
BALLIGI.eng_example: He was the one who was victorious in the race.

BALLIKUG.definition: To modify, distort, or pervert (what someone has said).
BALLIKUG.eng_example: He modified what I told him.

BALLOLONG.definition: To place hands that are joined around the head.

BALNAS.definition: To rinse in water, especially dishes that have been soaped.

BALO.definition: to cause (someone) to become a widow or widower.

BALO.ilok_example: Nabalo diay barok idi napalabas nga tawen.
BALO.eng_example: My son was widowed the past year.

BALO.definition: to make or dig holes in the ground with a stake for posts or plants.
BALO.eng_example: They went to make holes in the ground with a stake.

BALO.definition: 1. to cause to step or fall into a hole. 2. to cause to sink deeply in (debt, hardships, etc.).
BALO.ilok_example: Sika ti mangibalo kanyak iti utang.
BALO.eng_example: You are going to cause me to sink deeply in debt.

BALO.definition: 1. to step or fall into a hole. 2. to sink deeply in (debt, hardships, etc.).

BALON.definition: provision, supply; something provided, prepared or supplied for the future.
to have or carry as provision, to provide oneself with.
BALON.eng_example: Provide yourself with something for us to eat.

BALON.definition: to carry provisions or supplies to.
BALON.eng_example: It was he who carried provisions to us.

BALOT.definition: duck’s egg with a developed embryo that is cooked and eaten.

BALOTA.definition: ballot, especially one used in an election.

BALSIG.eng_example: I’ll go chop what we are going to use as firewood.

BALTIK.definition: to flip, flick or fillip something at.
BALTIK.ilok_example: Saan mo nga baltiken dagita ubbing.
BALTIK.eng_example: Don’t fillip something at those children.

BALTIK.definition: to flip, flick or fillip (something) at.

BALUBAL.definition: to be rivals, to be set against each other.
BALUBAL.ilok_example: Agbalubal ti ili mi ken ti ili da.
BALUBAL.eng_example: Our town and their town are rivals.

BALUD.eng_example: Why did they confine you in prison?

BALUDBUD.definition: growing vigorously, robust, healthy, as a person or a plant.

BALUKNIT.ilok_example: Baluknitem dayta bituka sa mo dalusan.
BALUKNIT.eng_example: Turn that stomach inside out and then clean it.

BALUNGYAD.definition: to move or push backward (a finger, a toe, the head, etc.).
BALUNGYAD.ilok_example: Saan mo nga balungyaden ta ramay ko.

BAMBAN.definition: a strip of young and pliant bamboo used for tying.

BANAAL.definition: having the stench of feces or excrement.

BANABA.definition: a kind of tree (Lagerstroemia speciosa (L.) Pers.).

BANAG.ilok_example: Kasta ti aramiden yo no adda mapidut yo a banag, ubbing.
BANAG.eng_example: That is what you should do when you pick up any object, children.

BANARBAR.definition: the sound of broken bells or of a broken voice.
to sound like broken bells or a broken voice.

BANBANNOG.eng_example: That will be a useless effort of yours.

BANDILI.definition: the fine-toothed blade of a hack saw or coping saw.

BANEG.ilok_example: Nabaneg dagiti ima ti kapitan nga nangtengngel kadagiti abaga ni Andres.
BANEG.eng_example: The hands of the captain which held the shoulders of Andrew were strong.

BANEGBEG.definition: to make a regular thumping sound, to pound or knock on something regularly.
BANEGBEG.ilok_example: Mangngeg ko nga agbanegbeg dagiti al-o da.
BANEGBEG.eng_example: I hear their pestles pounding regularly.
It was he who pounded on the gate.

BANERBER.definition: the sound of a swollen river, a strong wind or the like.
to sound like a swollen river, a strong wind or the like.

BANESBES.definition: to rush, whish; to move with a whish especially when moving fast.

BANG-AR.eng_example: I am cheered to see you.

BANG-I.definition: having the smell of toast or broiled fish.

BANGA.definition: earthen or clay pot, especially one used to cook rice in.

BANGABANGA.definition: to swarm in a heap: said of bugs, bees, etc.
BANGABANGA.eng_example: The bugs are swarming in a heap.

BANGAD.definition: back of a knife, a saw, etc.

BANGAR.definition: a spreading tree with rank-smelling flowers (Sterculia foetida, L.).

BANGBANGIR.definition: one half of anything (e.g. a squash); derivative of BANGIR.

BANGBANGLO.definition: perfume, cologne; derivative of BANGLO / PABANGLO.

BANGBANGSIT.definition: A common foul-smelling herbal plant, such as Lantana camara (kantutay) or Hyptis suaveolens; derivative of BANGSIT.

BANGEG.definition: having a hoarse, low-pitched, bass or deep voice or sound.
BANGEG.eng_example: Your teacher has a low-pitched voice.

BANGEN.definition: a fence-like device placed at the doorsill to prevent small children from getting out of the room.

BANGGA.definition: Collision; to collide with (dialectal variant of BANGDOL).

BANGGAL.definition: to tie a handkerchief or a similar piece of material around the crown of one’s head, folding it diagonally and knotting the ends in front so as to form a kind of cone.
BANGGAL.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agbanggal ta napudot.
BANGGAL.eng_example: Don’t tie a handkerchief around the crown of your head for it is warm.

BANGGAL.definition: to tie around the crown of one’s head.
BANGGAL.eng_example: Who tied my handkerchief around the crown of his head?

BANGGERA.definition: place in the kitchen or adjoining the kitchen where the plates, glasses, silverware, etc. are washed, drained, and stacked.

BANGIBANG.definition: to be adjacent, contiguous, next to each other, close to each other.
BANGIBANG.ilok_example: Agbangibang ti ili mi ken ti ili da.
BANGIBANG.eng_example: Our town and their town are adjacent.

BANGIBANG.definition: one that is adjacent or close.
BANGIBANG.eng_example: They are the ones who are adjacent to us.

BANGIR.definition: to go or transfer to the other side.
to use the other side for doing something.

BIAG.ilok_example: Narigat ti biag ditoy ili mi.
BIAG.eng_example: Life is hard in our town.

BIAG.definition: To live, remain alive, live on.
BIAG.eng_example: Do you think what I planted is going to live?

BIAG.definition: 1. To make live or survive. 2. To revive.
BIAG.eng_example: I was the one who made you live.

BIAHE.definition: To travel, to make a trip or voyage.
1. To transport to another place in order to sell. 2. To take on a trip.
BIAHE.eng_example: I will transport corn to Manila to sell.

BIAHERO.definition: One who is fond of traveling, one who travels a lot.

BIANG.definition: To concern oneself with, to interfere with, meddle in.
BIANG.ilok_example: Saan mo nga biangan ti ania man nga aramiden na.
BIANG.eng_example: Don’t concern yourself with anything that he does.

BIBINGKA.definition: 1. A kind of thick, flat, and round cake made of glutinous rice (DIKET). 2. A kind of flat and round cake made of non-glutinous rice, thinner and smaller than the BIKO.

BIDA.definition: Hero or heroine in a movie, the leading star in a movie.

BIDANG.definition: A broad band or sash worn by women around the body from the waist to the knee.
To put a bidang sash around someone.

phrases.phrase: Liniklikan na ti biddut na idi napalabas nga bulan.
phrases.translation: He avoided his mistakes last month.

BIDING.ilok_example: Bidingen yo nga nalaing dayta lupot tapno makita yo amin nga rugit na.
BIDING.eng_example: Inspect well that cloth so that you can see all its dirt.

BIGAO.definition: A large, circular or oval, shallow basket made of closely woven strips of bamboo, used principally as a winnowing basket.

BIGAT.definition: Morning, the period of the day between sunrise and noon.

phrases.translation: Someday in the future / Any time now.

BIGBIG.ilok_example: Ammo na ti agbigbig dayta anak mon.
BIGBIG.eng_example: Your child already knows how to recognize people.

BIGBIG.ilok_example: Saan nak nga bigbigen nga inam.
BIGBIG.eng_example: Don’t acknowledge me as your mother.

BIGBIG.definition: To be able to recognize; to discover.
BIGBIG.eng_example: They were not able to recognize me.

BIGLA.definition: To surprise, startle by doing something suddenly and unexpectedly.
BIGLA.ilok_example: Saan mo nga biglaen ta dinto ket agsakit.
BIGLA.eng_example: Don’t startle him for he might get sick.

BIIT.definition: To be brief or short in duration, to be away or stay for a short while.
Brief, short in duration (in the past).
The generic name for early rice.
To do briefly or within a short time.
BIIT.ilok_example: Binibiit na nga inibus diay dugo.
BIIT.eng_example: He consumed the broth within a short time.

BIKAL.definition: 1. A climbing bamboo with thick walls. 2. A stake made of this.

BIKKIAS.ilok_example: Irutem ti galut na dayta karton tapno saan nga bumikkias.
BIKKIAS.eng_example: Tighten the binding of that cardboard box so that it won’t burst open.

BIKO.definition: Native cake made of sticky rice, coconut milk, and brown sugar cooked in a big, round, and shallow pan.

BIKS.definition: Vicks ointment or any other similar ointment.

BILADA.eng_example: I will dance during the celebration.

BILAG.definition: A sunny place, a place hit directly by the rays of the sun.
BILAG.ilok_example: Saan ka nga aggian dita bilag.
BILAG.eng_example: Don’t stay in that sunny place.

BILAG.definition: To stay under the sun, to sunbathe.
BILAG.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agbilag ta dinto agsakit ka.
BILAG.eng_example: Don’t stay under the sun for you might get sick.

BILAG.definition: To place under the sun, to dry under the sun.
BILAG.ilok_example: Mapan na ibilag dagidiay nilabaan na.
BILAG.eng_example: She will go dry under the sun what she washed.

BILANG.eng_example: What is their number? or: How many are they?

BILANG.definition: To count, to recite the numbers in succession.
BILANG.eng_example: I still don’t know how to count.
I consider you as my friend.

BILID.definition: The peak of an angle, top of the end formed by an angle.

BILIN.ilok_example: Bilinem bassit dayta anak mo, sa ka mapan.
BILIN.eng_example: Counsel your child a little and then go.

BILIN.definition: To instruct or request to get, buy, do, etc.
BILIN.eng_example: What did you request him to buy?

BILOG.definition: A small boat made of the hollowed-out trunk of a tree, or of boards put together, having two outriggers; it is much larger than the BARANGAY.

BIMMAKKA.definition: Of the size and shape of a BAKKA: said especially of the vulva.

BIN-I.definition: Seedling, seeds kept for the next planting season.

BINABAI.definition: A capon, a castrated rooster, especially one fattened for eating.

BINAKLAG.definition: To swell or become swollen due to bites or other injuries.
BINAKLAG.eng_example: These ones bitten by mosquitoes became swollen.

BINATOG.ilok_example: Nailanad daytoy nga binatog iti libro.
BINATOG.eng_example: This line was written in the book.

BINGAY.definition: To give as one’s share, to share with.
BINGAY.ilok_example: Ibingay mo man la kanyak dayta bunga ti tarong yon?
BINGAY.eng_example: Will you please just give me that fruit of your eggplant as my share?

BINGGAS.definition: Fiber of the body; grain of wood; white vein or streak of the betel nut.

BINGIT.definition: To stretch open, especially with the hands.

BINGKOL.definition: Clod, a lump of earth which is hard and dry.

BINGNGI.ilok_example: Umisem ka inggana ti agbingngi ti bibig mo.
BINGNGI.eng_example: Smile until your lips break open.

BINOKBOK.definition: A tooth with a cavity, a tooth with caries.

BINTING.definition: Twenty-five centavos, a quarter of a peso.
BINTING.eng_example: My money is only twenty-five centavos.

BINTOR.definition: To roam around, wander about, rove.
BINTOR.ilok_example: Isu ti nagbintor nga agsapul kenkuana.
BINTOR.eng_example: He was the one who wandered about looking for him.

BINUBUDAN.definition: Cooked rice (usually non-glutinous) sprinkled with yeast (BUBUD) and left in a cool place to ferment for one or two days; fermented rice.

BINUGBOG.definition: Leftovers kept to feed the pigs.
BINUGBOG.ilok_example: Naimas nga binugbog ti ipakan na iti baboy na.
BINUGBOG.eng_example: He will feed his pig with tasty leftovers.

BIOR.definition: 1. To control, cause to submit to one’s authority. 2. To bend, e.g. a wire, a piece of bamboo, wood, etc.
BIOR.ilok_example: Narigat nga mabior daytoy nga ubing.
BIOR.eng_example: It is hard to control this child.

BIR-I.definition: To develop or have a crack.
BIR-I.eng_example: The plate which was dropped developed a crack.

BIRABID.definition: An edible, freshwater, gastropodous mollusk with a round, thin shell.
To feel dizzy and feverish due to eating birabid.
BIRABID.ilok_example: Saan mo nga kaaduen ti mangan ti dayta ta dikanto mabirabid.
BIRABID.eng_example: Don’t eat much of that for you might feel dizzy and feverish afterwards.

BIRAY.definition: A small boat made of boards and with a flat bottom, which is used for long distances; it is much larger than the BARANGAY.

BIRIA.definition: To patch; to mend, cover, or fill up a hole, crack, or weak spot.
BIRIA.eng_example: Patch that crack of the jar.

BIRIT.definition: A scar or scarlike indentation on the eyelid.

BIRKUG.definition: Derelict, negligent, being a regular absentee.
BIRKUG.ilok_example: Maysa ka nga hues nga birkug.

BIRNGAS.definition: 1. To call by one’s nickname or first name. 2. To call or address impolitely.
BIRNGAS.ilok_example: Saan mo nga birbirngasen ni tatang ko.
BIRNGAS.eng_example: Don’t call my father by his nickname.

BIROK.ilok_example: Birokem daydiay lapis ko nga napukaw.
BIROK.eng_example: Look for my pencil which was lost.

BIROK.definition: To be able to find; to find by chance.
BIROK.ilok_example: Indiak nga mabirokan diay lapis mo.

BIRTUD.definition: Potent, effective: said of medicine or poison.

BIRUT.definition: A kind of small freshwater fish.

BISALEG.definition: To have an acute pain: said of the abdomen or stomach.
BISALEG.eng_example: My stomach has an acute pain.

BISIBIS.definition: To sprinkle or spray with water or any other liquid.
BISIBIS.ilok_example: Bisibisam dayta dalikan tapno maepdep amin nga apoy na.
BISIBIS.eng_example: Sprinkle the stove with water so that the fire in it will be put out.

BISIBIS.definition: To sprinkle or spray in or on.
BISIBIS.ilok_example: Daytoy ti ibisbis mo idiay dalikan.

BISIK.ilok_example: Isu ti nangibisik iti gagara na.
BISIK.eng_example: He was the one who revealed his mission.

BISIKLETA.definition: To use a bicycle, to ride on a bicycle.

BISIN.ilok_example: Adu nga tao ti agbisin ita umay nga bulan.
BISIN.eng_example: Many people will go hungry this coming month.

BISIN.definition: To cause or allow to go hungry, to starve.
BISIN.ilok_example: Saan mo nga bisbisinen dayta bagim.
BISIN.eng_example: Don’t allow yourself to go hungry.

BISIN.definition: To suffer hunger, to go hungry.
BISIN.eng_example: I went hungry waiting for you.

BISIO.ilok_example: Nagadu la ket ti bisio mon.

BISIO.definition: Having many vices, idiosyncracies, or eccentricities.
BISIO.ilok_example: Nabisio la unay dayta lakay mo.

BISIRO.definition: Young male of the horse, pony.

BISITA.ilok_example: Agsubli tayo ta adda bisita da.
BISITA.eng_example: Let’s go back for they have a visitor.

BISITA.ilok_example: Bisitaen nak met uray man no sagpaminsan laeng.
BISITA.eng_example: Please visit me even if only once in a while.

BISLIN.definition: To press or squeeze oneself in.
BISLIN.ilok_example: Bumislin ka dita ta awan ti lugar mo ditoyen.
BISLIN.eng_example: Squeeze in there for you have no space here now.

BISLIN.ilok_example: Isu ti nangibislin ti bagi na ditoy.
BISLIN.eng_example: It was he who squeezed himself in here.

BISNGAR.definition: To turn up because of anger: said of the nose.
BISNGAR.ilok_example: Uray la nga nagbisngar ti agong na ti pungtot na.
BISNGAR.eng_example: His nose turned up because of his anger.

BISNGIT.definition: To part, push aside to make an opening.
BISNGIT.ilok_example: Bisngitem dayta sanga ta mula tapno makitam ida.
BISNGIT.eng_example: Push aside that branch of that plant so that you can see them.

BISSAYOT.ilok_example: Sep-akem dayta sanga ti kayo tapno agbissayot ditoy daga.
BISSAYOT.eng_example: Break that branch of the tree so that it will hang downwards to the ground.

BISSAYOT.definition: To keep aloft holding by the neck, hand or feet; to suspend in the air.
BISSAYOT.ilok_example: Saan mo nga bissayoten dayta pusa.
BISSAYOT.eng_example: Don’t suspend the cat in the air.

BISTI.eng_example: Dress yourself for we are going.

BISTI.ilok_example: Bistiam dayta ubing ta adda papanan mi.
BISTI.eng_example: Dress that child for we are going somewhere.

BISTRAD.definition: 1. To spread out, as a piece of cloth. 2. To open, lay open, as a book, the eyes, etc.

BISUKOL.definition: A kind of snail with a smooth round shell.

BITAY.definition: To hang by the neck until dead.

BITIBIT.definition: To carry or hold in the hand hanging or dangling.
BITIBIT.eng_example: He held the chicken in his hand dangling.

BITIK.definition: To palpitate, throb: said of the heart or the chest.
BITIK.ilok_example: Agbitikbitik ti barukong na ti pannakakigtot na.
BITIK.eng_example: His chest is palpitating due to his being surprised.

BITIN.definition: To suspend oneself, to hang or remain suspended.
BITIN.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agbitin dita sanga ti kayo.
BITIN.eng_example: Don’t hang on the branch of that tree.

BITIN.ilok_example: Ibitin mo daytoy karne idiay adigi.
BITIN.eng_example: Hang this meat on the post.

BITINBITIN.definition: Something hanging, especially for a purpose.

BITLA.definition: To discourse, deliver a speech or address.
BITLA.ilok_example: Isu ti nagbitla idi pabuya mi.
BITLA.eng_example: He was the one who delivered an address during our show.

BITTAUG.definition: 1. A tall tree which yields timber. 2. A fruit of this tree.

BITTAYON.definition: To hang or dangle downwards (out of an opening).
BITTAYON.ilok_example: Adda makitak nga agbittayon nga ima dita tawa.
BITTAYON.eng_example: I see a hand dangling from that window.

BOA.definition: 1. The betel-nut or areca-nut palm (Areca catechu L.). 2. A fruit of this palm.

BOBONG.definition: 1. The thatch that covers the ridge of a roof; hence, 2. The ridge of a roof.

BOBONGAN.definition: The two beams at the ridge of the roof: the SALLABAWAN and the PAKABAYO.

BOGBOG.definition: 1. To cause to become pulpy, e.g. by cooking to excess or by beating; hence, 2. To maul, hit or beat repeatedly.
1. To be caused to become pulpy. 2. To be mauled, hit or beaten repeatedly.

BOKA.ilok_example: Siguro agbuka dayta nalabaga nga sabong inton bigat.
BOKA.eng_example: Maybe that red flower will open tomorrow.

BOKA.definition: 1. To untie, unbind, unfasten, undo, loosen (a knot). 2. To let loose or set free; to let go.
BOKA.ilok_example: Saan mo nga bokaen dayta galut ti aso.
BOKA.eng_example: Don’t untie the leash of the dog.

phrases.phrase: Saan mo nga bokaen dayta aso nga naungit.
phrases.translation: Don’t let loose that fierce dog.

BOKBOK.definition: Weevil or its larva; powder post beetle; woodworm.
To be attacked by weevils: said of posts, boards, bamboos, etc.

BOKRA.definition: To untie or undo (a knot); to unravel or untangle (a tangle).
BOKRA.ilok_example: Bokraem man daytoy siglot ti talik?
BOKRA.eng_example: Will you please untie this knot in my rope?

BOLA.definition: 1. Ball, any round object; sphere; globe. 2. Any game using a ball.
To play a game with a ball, especially baseball.
BOLA.eng_example: Let’s play a game with a ball.

BOLABOLA.definition: 1. A ball of sewing thread usually wound on a bobbin. 2. Anything that is rounded, e.g. meatballs.

BOONG.ilok_example: Saan mo nga boongen dayta baso.

BOONG.definition: To be or get broken, fractured, cracked.
BOONG.ilok_example: Nadaras nga maboong dayta baso yo.

BOOS.definition: A kind of large, red, stinging ant whose eggs are edible.

BOOT.definition: To be attacked by mold or mildew.

BOTOS.definition: To vote, to cast one’s vote.

BRIAT.definition: To rip, tear, or split open or apart.
BRIAT.eng_example: He was the one who ripped my clothes.

BRIAT.definition: To be ripped, torn, or split apart or open; to suffer a tear.

BRUHA.definition: An evil woman, a witch or sorceress.

BUAL.ilok_example: Saan mo man nga bualen dayta mulak.
BUAL.eng_example: Please don’t cause my plant to fall down.

BUANG.definition: 1. To open, remove the plug of. 2. To set loose.
To let (newly hatched chicks) out of the nest.
BUANG.eng_example: You let the chicks out of the nest.

BUANGAY.definition: To do by oneself, be responsible for.
BUANGAY.ilok_example: Isu ti nangbuangay iti daytoy nga pabuya.
BUANGAY.eng_example: He was responsible for this show.

BUAT.definition: To help (someone) lift a load on someone’s head or shoulder.
BUAT.eng_example: Will you please help me lift this load on my head?

BUAT.definition: To lift (a load) on the head or shoulder of.
BUAT.eng_example: It is hard to lift that jar on the head of someone.

BUBO.definition: A kind of large or small bow net made of bamboo which is used to catch freshwater shrimps or fish.

BUBO.ilok_example: Saan mo nga ibubo dayta ubing.
BUBO.eng_example: Don’t expose that child to the wind.

BUBO.definition: To be exposed to the wind.
BUBO.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agtugaw dita ta maibubo ka.
BUBO.eng_example: Don’t sit there for you will be exposed to the wind.

BUBON.definition: Well, a hole sunk into the earth to reach a supply of water.

BUBUBUDO.definition: A kind of large, soft, black or dark-brown, hairy, stinging caterpillar.

BUDO.definition: Hair on wormlike larvae or plants and fruits.

BUDO.eng_example: What caused you to become itchy?

BUDO.ilok_example: Nabudoan diay balasang idi nagdigos idiay karayan.
BUDO.eng_example: The young lady was infected by itchiness when she bathed in the river.

BUELTA.definition: To turn back, head back, return.
To turn something back; to take, drive, or cause to go back.

BUGAS.definition: 1. Pith of plant stems. 2. Core of fruits.
To develop its core: said of fruits.

BUGAYONG.definition: 1. A slender, leguminous vine with seeds which are half black and half scarlet. 2. A seed of this plant.

BUGGO.definition: To wash one’s hands or limbs.
To wash (the hands or limbs of).

BUGGOONG.definition: Fish preserved in salt and slightly fermented and used as sauce.

BUGI.definition: The ovary or eggs of fishes, crabs, lobsters, shrimps, etc.

BUGKAW.definition: To shout, yell, or bawl at.
BUGKAW.ilok_example: Binugkawan na diay ubing nga natagari.
BUGKAW.eng_example: He bawled at the noisy child.

BUGNAY.definition: A kind of tree which bears round, acidic, edible fruits which turn red when ripe.

BUGSOT.definition: To convulse, as when near death.
BUGSOT.eng_example: I am already convulsing still you don’t come to help me.

phrases.phrase: Saan nak man nga bugtaken ta adu ti trabahok.
phrases.translation: Please don’t disturb me for I have much work to do.

BUIS.definition: Tax paid to the government on incomes and properties.
To pay taxes to the government.

BUISIT.definition: Unlucky, having bad luck (as in gambling).
1. To cause someone to be unlucky or have bad luck (as in gambling). 2. To irritate, pester.

BUKAIT.definition: To open slightly by prying, e.g. a package.

BUKAR.ilok_example: Saan pay nga naloom dayta ta di pay nagbukar.
BUKAR.eng_example: That one is not ripe yet for it has not yet burst open.

BUKATOT.definition: A kind of basket similar in shape to a demijohn made of woven strips of bamboo and used for holding fish by fishermen.

BUKAYKAY.definition: To rip or cut open and spill out the contents of.
BUKAYKAY.eng_example: He cut open the pillow and spilled out its contents.

BUKAYKAY.definition: To be ripped causing its contents to spill out: said of pillows, sacks of rice, etc.
BUKAYKAY.eng_example: His pillow was ripped and its contents spilled out.

BUKAYO.definition: A kind of sweet made of coconut meat and sugar.

BUKBOK.definition: To spill or flow out by accident.
BUKBOK.ilok_example: Naibukbok diay danom nga pagdigos mo.
BUKBOK.eng_example: The water for your bath spilled out by accident.

BUKEL.definition: To be formed, conceived; to take form.
BUKEL.ilok_example: Nagbukel daytoy nga panunot iti isip na.
BUKEL.eng_example: This thought took form in his mind.

BUKEL.definition: To form, conceive of, e.g. a thought, project, etc.
1. Round and solid (as an object). 2. Loud and clear (as voice).
BUKEL.ilok_example: Nabukel ti panagbalikas na iti nagan na.
BUKEL.eng_example: The way he uttered his name was loud and clear.

BUKIBUK.ilok_example: Saan mo nga bukibuken dagita nalabaan.
BUKIBUK.eng_example: Don’t turn over the washed clothes.

BUKINGKING.definition: To hit with the back of the hand.

BUKIRAD.definition: 1. To open wide, dilate (as the eyes do). 2. To break or burst (like a seed, kernel or grain).

BUKITKIT.definition: To look for something through the contents of or inside (a box, a book, etc.) with the hand.

BUKKUAL.ilok_example: Bukkualem dayta daga ta ibunubon mo dagitoy bukel ti tarong.
BUKKUAL.eng_example: Turn up the soil and sow these eggplant seeds.

BUKLAN.definition: Seedy, filled with seeds; derivative of BUKEL.

BUKO.definition: 1. Knuckle. 2. Node of plants or something similar to this. 3. Bud.

BUKOD.definition: To be alone, stay alone, live alone.

BUKOD.ilok_example: Bimmukod ni Pedro kadaydiay pamilya na.
BUKOD.eng_example: Pedro lived separately from his family.

BUKOD.definition: To take or do by oneself excluding others; to monopolize.
BUKOD.eng_example: He did all the work by himself excluding the others from it.

BUKOL.definition: Hump, bump; a protuberance, a swelling.
To cause to have a bump; to strike or knock with force so as to produce a hump.

BUKOT.definition: Back (of a person, an animal, a book, etc.).

BUKSIL.definition: The outer cover or integument of seeds.
To remove the outer cover or integument of seeds.
BUKSIL.eng_example: Remove the integument of my seed.

BUKSIL.definition: To explain, state succinctly, e.g. one’s desires.

BUKSIT.definition: Abdomen; belly, especially around the umbilical region.

BUKTO.definition: A kind of small, whitish, freshwater fish.

BULANG.definition: To go to a cockfight, to engage in cockfighting, to match one’s gamecock with that of another in a cockpit.
BULANG.eng_example: I will go to a cockfight in your town.

BULANG.definition: To match (a gamecock) in a cockfight.

BULANGAN.definition: Cockpit, a place where cockfighting is done.

BULANOS.ilok_example: Maupayak nga makaammo iti kaawan ti nabulanos nga tulong dagiti dadduma nga ili.
BULANOS.eng_example: I am disappointed to know about the lack of spontaneous help from the other towns.

BULBULLAGAW.definition: A clown, jester, joker; a funny person.

BULDING.definition: To blind in one eye, to injure or destroy an eye of.

BULDOSER.definition: To use a bulldozer on; to bulldoze.

BULIBUL.definition: Remuneration in kind for work done, payment in kind.
To receive (something other than money) for work done, to earn (something other than money).
BULIBUL.ilok_example: Adu ti nabulibul ko idi napalabas nga bulan.
BULIBUL.eng_example: I earned much (in kind) the past month.

BULIG.ilok_example: Agbulig kayo ti dayta nadagsen nga kahon.

BULIG.definition: One whole stem or cluster of banana fruits; this consists of several rows or hands of bananas each one called SAPAD.

BULINTIK.definition: A children’s game played with marbles; marbles.
To play marbles with each other.

BULLO.definition: To have a bone broken or a joint dislocated; to have a sprain; hence, to be crippled or disabled.
To break a bone or dislocate a joint of; to sprain; hence, to cripple or disable.

BULO.definition: A slender, erect, thornless bamboo whose walls are thin.

BULOD.eng_example: May I borrow some of your salt.

BULOG.definition: Male progenitor; uncastrated male carabao, pig, etc.

BULOS.ilok_example: Saan da nga ibulbulos dayta nga aso.
BULOS.eng_example: They don’t let that dog loose.

BULOS.ilok_example: Nagbulos di dara diay sugat na.
BULOS.eng_example: The blood from his wound flowed freely and profusely.

BULOS.definition: To emit or flow from freely and profusely.
BULOS.ilok_example: Adu nga dara ti imbulos diay sugat na.
BULOS.eng_example: Much blood flowed freely from his wound.

BULSA.definition: To put or keep inside one’s pocket.
BULSA.eng_example: Put this banana of mine inside your pocket.

BULSEK.definition: Totally blind; blind in both eyes.

BUMALASANG.definition: 1. Young woman below or at the age of puberty and usually though not necessarily unmarried; girl. 2. Young female of the water buffalo or cow.

BUMARO.definition: 1. Young man below or at the age of puberty and usually though not necessarily unmarried; boy. 2. Young male of the water buffalo or cow; pony.
To be near or at the age of puberty: said of the male.

BUMBA.definition: To pump, especially a pump well (POSO).

BUMBA.ilok_example: Bumbaen diay eroplano daytoy balay tayo.
BUMBA.eng_example: The airplane will bomb our house.

BUNAG.definition: To transport, to carry from one place to another.
BUNAG.ilok_example: Bunagen yo man dagitoy alikamen mi?
BUNAG.eng_example: Will you please transport our belongings?

BUNG-OR.definition: To become swollen and tender due to an injury or infection.

BUNGA.definition: 1. Fruit; result. 2. Child (a term of endearment used especially in literary works).

BUNGA.eng_example: Our mango tree is now bearing fruits.

BUNGA.definition: To bear, result in, lead to.
BUNGA.ilok_example: Adu ti bungaen dayta mangga yo.
BUNGA.eng_example: That mango tree of yours will bear many fruits.

BUNGA.definition: To have or develop a sty.
BUNGA.eng_example: The man’s eye is developing a sty.

BUNGABONG.ilok_example: Inbungabong na ti gandat na nga agkandidato.
BUNGABONG.eng_example: He announced his intention to run as a candidate.

BUNGAW.definition: Having one or both testicles swollen or enlarged; having scrotal hernia.

BUNGDOL.definition: With tipless or blunt horn, as a cow or water buffalo.

BUNGGOY.eng_example: They are the ones he associated with.

BUNGLUG.definition: Having the stench of rancid oil, lard, etc.

BUNGON.definition: To wrap, bundle, package; to bundle up.
BUNGON.ilok_example: Bungonem nga nalaing dayta anak mo ta lumamiis manen.
BUNGON.eng_example: Bundle up your child well for it is getting cold again.

BUNGSOT.definition: To cause to rot, become spoiled, putrid, foul.

BUNGULAN.definition: A kind of yellow, spotted, fragrant banana.

BUNOT.definition: The outer husk of the coconut; coir.

BUNTIEK.definition: The young of the fish called DALAG.

BUNUBON.definition: Seedling, a plant grown from a seed for transplanting.
To grow plants from seeds for transplanting; to sow seeds for seedlings.
BUNUBON.eng_example: We can sow seeds for seedlings now.

BUNYAG.definition: To baptize someone especially in church.

BUNYAG.ilok_example: Daydiay lakay nga padi ti mangbunyag ti anak ko.
BUNYAG.eng_example: It is the old priest who will baptize my child.

BUNYAG.definition: To give or bestow on as a name or alias.
BUNYAG.eng_example: This is what he bestowed on me as an alias.

To be crushed, shattered, broken into pieces.
To shake in order to collect the fish, shrimps, crabs, etc. caught in a submerged branch pile (fagot).

BURANG-IT.definition: To raise one’s bottom or buttocks, to set oneself in a position with the bottom or buttocks up.

BURARAWIT.definition: A long slender branch; a pendulous top of the bamboo.

BURAYOK.definition: To flow profusely, to gush out.
BURAYOK.ilok_example: Nagburayok ti dara diay sugat na.
BURAYOK.eng_example: The blood of his wound gushed out.

BURBUR.definition: Down, soft fluffy hair, furry hair.

BURBURAN.definition: 1. A kind of spaniel, poodle or Pekinese dog with long, thick wavy hair. 2. A kind of shaggy blanket.

BUSBUS.definition: To loosen, slacken; to make loose or slack.
BUSBUS.ilok_example: Apay nga busbusem dayta galut ti kahon?
BUSBUS.eng_example: Why are you making the binding of the box loose?

BUSBUS.ilok_example: Irutem dayta galut ti kahon tapno saan nga mabusbus.
BUSBUS.eng_example: Tighten the band of the box so that it will not become loose.

BUSEL.definition: 1. Flower bud of pistillate flowers. 2. Young coconut, melon, squash, etc.

BUSI.definition: To pop, as corn or rice.

BUSLON.definition: To waste; to use much more than necessary.

BUSNAG.definition: Light-colored, fair in complexion: said of a person.

BUSSOG.definition: To fill oneself with food, to satiate oneself with food.
BUSSOG.ilok_example: Agbussog ka ta adayo ti papanan tayo.
BUSSOG.eng_example: Fill yourself with food for we are going far.

BUSSOG.definition: To fill or satiate with food, to feed until full.
BUSSOG.ilok_example: Saan mo nga busbussogen ta aso tapno di nga maturog.
BUSSOG.eng_example: Don’t fill that dog with food so that it will not go to sleep.

BUTBUT.definition: To put a hole on; to puncture.

BUTBUTENG.ilok_example: Awan ti butbuteng na nga napan idiay sementerio.
BUTBUTENG.eng_example: He went to the cemetery without fear.

BUTBUTENG.definition: Frightening, scary, alarming; causing fear or fright.

BUTEG.definition: Like mucus: said especially of the meat of young coconuts or betel nuts.

BUTENG.definition: To be afraid of, scared of, frightened by; to dread, fear.

BUTILAW.definition: A protrusion of the uterus into the vagina.

BUTINGGAN.definition: Wild tomato whose fruits are small, round, and smooth-skinned.

BUTO.definition: 1. Penis. 2. Style of the pistil. 3. Tongue of a bell.

BUYOK.definition: Fetid, having a bad smell; stinking.

BUYUBOY.definition: A kind of cup or dipper made of coconut shell.
